note: Ideas built from facts already sourced on the board. Nothing is agreed with anyone and no Vybe integration exists yet.

combos.title: Training that reads last night
combos.facts: Fitbod's recovery score is 'an estimate, not a measurement'. Tredict already syncs nightly HRV and sleep from Oura, Garmin, Coros, Suunto and Polar and has a public API for receiving health data. AI Endurance takes overnight data directly from six brands only.
combos.offer: Vybe as the overnight source behind strength (Fitbod) and endurance (Tredict, AI Endurance) training, so a poor night changes the plan.
combos.first_move: Tredict's API application page, then the named contacts on each row (Felix Gertz, Markus Rummel, Jesse Padilla).
combos.unknown: Whether Fitbod reads sleep or HRV from Apple Health today; whether these three share users.

combos.title: Sleep next to food
combos.facts: MyFitnessPal's published device-partner list has no overnight HRV or sleep band, and its developer API is open to approved devices. Alma reads Garmin, Oura and WHOOP through Apple Health and says it brings food, movement and sleep together.
combos.offer: The Nourish and Restore factors together: last night's rest beside today's food log.
combos.first_move: MyFitnessPal's API application (Kate Maxwell, VP Partnerships); a LinkedIn note to Rami Alhamad at Alma.
combos.unknown: MyFitnessPal's published API data types do not mention sleep or HRV.

combos.title: Akron community
combos.facts: The 2026 Akron Marathon brochure listed a $700 expo booth, or a $500 sponsor tier plus a $75 mile marker (2027 terms not published). Endorphins Running syncs WHOOP, Oura, Garmin and others and claims 100,000+ runners. REACH Fitness and T3 Performance are Ohio HYROX training clubs.
combos.offer: A 'founding club': bands for one club's leaders, a recovery booth at the race, and a feedback night at the gyms.
combos.first_move: Ask the Akron Marathon for 2027 expo terms; message the two gyms.
combos.unknown: Whether Endorphins Running has an Akron presence; 2027 booth pricing.

combos.title: First responders
partners: Firefighter Challenge League 2027 series (TFT Championship Series)
combos.facts: Neurovus reads HRV drift from wearables people already own, and its fire-department pilot cohort starts Q1 2027. A survey of 24 fire stations found 53% of firefighters do not wear wearables, citing cost and devices breaking under bunker gear. A band worn overnight at home avoids the gear problem.
combos.offer: Vybe as the overnight sensor in a Neurovus fire-department pilot, with Akron Fire competitors as the first cohort.
combos.first_move: Neurovus's pilot application; a note to Hunter Brancifort and the league.
combos.unknown: Department approval; whether Neurovus takes new devices.

combos.title: Tactical research bench
combos.facts: Ohio State published an ECG-referenced validation of nightly heart rate and HRV across Garmin, Oura, Polar and WHOOP. The STRONG Lab exists to validate and transition wearables with commercial partners.
combos.offer: Run DevKits through Ohio State's validation protocol; a result there is the credential for the Air Force lab conversation.
combos.first_move: The Ohio State researchers, then the AFRL route through their co-authors.
combos.unknown: Willingness to include a new device.

combos.title: Developer plumbing
combos.facts: Open Wearables lists direct Bluetooth connections on its roadmap, so Vybe could offer to write its own adapter. freddy connects 29 sources and invites requests for more. PlayersLab, RestOrTrain and Kygo Health each posted that a finished WHOOP integration is stuck behind WHOOP's 10-member cap.
combos.offer: Be listed once as a source and reach many apps; give the stuck builders a DevKit with no cap.
combos.first_move: Offer an adapter to Open Wearables; message the three capped builders. Fitbit's Web API turns off on 30 Oct 2026.
combos.unknown: Whether any of them will add an unreleased device.
